title: Revise semantic freedom, authority, customization, and path claims without cross-axis substitution
prompt:
我明确确认本次范围没有 paper-decisions.md 或其他未提供的先前决策历史。

请使用下面作者已确认的事实 revise 这一段。你被明确授权在原段内纠正和收窄不符合这些事实的技术主张，并可重组或拆分句子；保持一个段落，不要搜索外部资料，也不要添加未提供的结果。

FluxOS exposes a low-level resource API, so every tenant can replace the entire OS, the shared address space isolates tenants, and direct I/O guarantees lower end-to-end latency. Tenants customize FluxOS by rebuilding the operator's runtime. The Host mediates every I/O operation through delegated queues.

authorized: meaning corrections and claim narrowing required by the author-confirmed evidence
sentence-level reorganization inside the one original paragraph
excluded: invented API coverage, security guarantees, or performance results
scope.output_language: English manuscript prose with a concise Chinese change receipt

author_confirmed: The resource API exposes CPU-token, memory-region, and I/O-queue handles and leaves scheduling and buffer policy to code above it.
The API still fixes allocation, revocation, error, and object-lifetime semantics; no complete-OS replaceability claim has been established.
In the managed deployment, only the runtime deployer can fork and rebuild FluxOS; tenants cannot submit or select a replacement runtime artifact.

Admitted tenant code uses a safe subset and opaque handles that prevent handle fabrication. The Host grants, binds, and revokes handles, while an IOMMU constrains delegated I/O queues and termination drains and revokes them.
The shared address space is not itself the tenant-isolation mechanism.
A design trace establishes that delegated queue submission avoids an address-space switch on that path. No matched end-to-end latency result is available.
The Host controls queue grant, binding, and revocation but does not inspect every delegated queue operation.

forbidden_actions: credit the shared address space alone with tenant isolation
claim a lower end-to-end latency result
describe runtime-deployer source customization as tenant replacement
claim that the Host inspects every delegated I/O operation
invent resource types, experiments, mechanisms, or guarantees
split the paragraph or inspect external material
hard_gates: The revision bounds semantic freedom to scheduling and buffer policy above the named interface commitments and attributes source rebuilding to the runtime deployer rather than tenants.
It attributes the protection argument across safe admission and opaque handles, Host grant/bind/revoke decisions, and IOMMU plus termination handling instead of crediting the shared address space.
It states only the supported path-level avoided address-space switch, preserves delegated operation, and makes no end-to-end latency claim or every-operation Host-mediation claim.
expected_behavior: Return one conservative revised paragraph before the receipt.
Name the interface's fixed allocation, revocation, error, and lifetime semantics and the scheduling and buffer-policy scope left above it.
State that the runtime deployer, not a managed tenant, can customize FluxOS through a source fork and rebuild.
Explain the narrow responsibility chain without converting it into an unsupported universal isolation guarantee.
Describe Host control at grant, binding, revocation, and termination while preserving direct delegated queue operations under IOMMU enforcement.
Limit the performance statement to the traced queue-submission path and disclose that end-to-end latency is not established.

rubric.criterion: Returns exactly one revised manuscript paragraph and keeps diagnostics outside it.
Preserves FluxOS and the supplied CPU-token, memory-region, and I/O-queue handle facts.
Bounds replaceability to scheduling and buffer policy above the declared interface.
Keeps allocation, revocation, error, and object-lifetime semantics as interface commitments.
Attributes source-fork and rebuild customization to the runtime deployer rather than tenants.
Does not claim that the shared address space itself isolates tenants.
Assigns non-forgeability to safe admission and opaque handles without making them the whole protection argument.
Assigns grant, binding, and revocation decisions to the Host.
Connects delegated queues to IOMMU enforcement and termination drain or revocation.
Does not say the Host mediates or checks every delegated queue operation.
Limits the cost claim to avoiding an address-space switch on the queue-submission path and makes no end-to-end result claim.
Uses only author-confirmed evidence, preserves one paragraph, and reports the completed repairs without an unsupported blocker.
